intent: Bring calc-live.zsh under the 250-line cap by extracting the warmed qalc coprocess into a sibling file, without changing what the live prompt calculator computes.
scope: Non-goal: changing the evaluator, the expression heuristic, or the ZLE bindings
changes: Moved the qalc coprocess block -- its four _CALC_Q* state variables and _calc_qalc_line, _calc_qco_start, _calc_qco_stop, _calc_qalc_eval -- into calc-live-qalc.zsh, sourced from calc-live.zsh after _CALC_QALC_BIN and _CALC_TIMEOUT_BIN are set.

The source line uses ${0:A:h}, the same idiom the file already relies on for _CALC_EVAL_PY. This matters here more than usual: the file is loaded as ~/.oh-my-zsh/custom/calc-live.zsh, a symlink into the repo, so a naive $0 would resolve into the oh-my-zsh custom directory where the sibling does not exist.

verification.command: zsh -c 'source ~/.oh-my-zsh/custom/calc-live.zsh; ...' -- through the real symlink, not the repo path
verification.evidence: Sources without error, all five probed functions are defined across the seam, _calc_eval '10/4' returns 2.5, and the qalc path in the NEW file works end to end: _calc_qalc_line '=5 ft to cm' strips to '5 ft to cm' and _calc_qalc_eval returns '152.4 cm'. This is the check that matters, since the symlink is how the file is actually loaded.

verification.command: seven expressions evaluated under HEAD and under the split, compared
verification.evidence: Identical for all seven: 2+2=4, 1/3=0.333333333333, sqrt(2)*3=4.24264068712, sin(pi/2)=1, 2^10=1024, 10/4=2.5, factorial(5)=120. _calc_is_expr still accepts '2+2' and still rejects 'ls -la', so ordinary commands remain untouched.
Both parse. zsh is the right parser here; shellcheck cannot read zsh syntax and the repo's shellcheck hook excludes zsh files, so the zsh-syntax hook is the gate.
calc-live.zsh 204, calc-live-qalc.zsh 74. Neither appears in the violation list.

verification.command: function-set and line-set diff against HEAD
verification.evidence: All ten functions preserved and identical. Zero executable lines lost; the single addition is the source line.

risks: This is a live interactive component: a broken source line would break every new shell, not just a script run on demand. That is why it was verified through the oh-my-zsh symlink rather than the repo path -- the symlink is the only path that actually exercises ${0:A:h}.

The coprocess variables are shared across the seam by design: calc-live-qalc.zsh sets _CALC_QRESULT and _CALC_QEXPR, which _calc_preview and _calc_accept_line in the main file read. This is a sourced-into-the-same-shell relationship, not two processes, and the end-to-end qalc test exercises exactly that path.

Already-running shells keep the old single-file version in memory until they exit; nothing needs restarting, but a shell opened mid-commit could source a half-written pair. Both files were written before either was staged.
rollback: git revert the commit; calc-live.zsh returns to its 266-line single-file form and the sibling disappears. No symlink change is needed -- the oh-my-zsh symlink points at calc-live.zsh either way.
After rollback, open a new shell and type '2+2' to confirm the live preview still appears.
